Tags: **[S]** primary public source, **[Y]** my synthesis, **[A]** simulation assumption. All trial data are simulated.

## (a) Concept

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Companion diagnostic (CDx) | Test essential for the safe and effective use of a specific medicine (selects patients, or flags risk) |
| Clinical trial assay (CTA) | The assay used to select/stratify patients in the pivotal drug trial; often not the final commercial IVD |
| Bridging study | Shows the final CDx classifies like the CTA, and translates the trial result to the CDx+ population |
| Concordance | PPA, NPA, OPA between CTA and CDx. **Not** sensitivity/specificity: neither assay is a reference |
| Enrichment design | Only biomarker-positive patients randomised: cannot assess benefit in biomarker-negatives |
| All-comers / stratified design | Everyone randomised, analysed by biomarker status; allows the treatment × biomarker interaction |

Core problem: the drug effect was estimated in *CTA-defined* patients, but patients will be selected by the *CDx*. If the two disagree, the effect in the CDx+ population is not what the trial reported, and the bridging set is usually **incomplete** (samples not retained). [Y]

## (b) Regulatory anchor

| Document | Verified statement | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| FDA, *In Vitro Companion Diagnostic Devices* (Aug 2014, final) | "An IVD companion diagnostic device is an in vitro diagnostic device that provides information that is essential for the safe and effective use of a corresponding therapeutic product." Footnote 10: most will be Class III, though a Class II/510(k) classification may be appropriate in some cases | [S] fda.gov/media/81309 |
| FDA, *Principles for Codevelopment of an IVD CDx with a Therapeutic Product* (July 2016) | **Still a draft** ("not for implementation") on FDA's page, content-current 2018 | [S] fda.gov/media/99030 |
| FDA, *Developing and Labeling IVD CDx for a Specific Group of Oncology Therapeutic Products* (Apr 2020, final) | The final title is "…Specific **Group** of…"; "Group or Class" was the draft title. Guidance body not read (landing page only) | [S] |
| IVDR Art 2(7) | CDx = device "essential for the safe and effective use of a corresponding medicinal product" to identify patients most likely to benefit, or at increased risk of serious adverse reactions | [S] |
| IVDR Annex VIII Rule 3(f) | CDx → **class C** | [S] |
| IVDR Art 48(7), 48(8) | For CDx the notified body consults "a competent authority … under Directive 2001/83/EC or the EMA, as applicable" (Annex IX 5.2 / Annex X 3(k)); also 48(3)/(4) for class D | [S] |
| IVDR Art 58(2) | CDx performance studies follow the additional-requirements articles; left-over-sample CDx studies are notified to the competent authority | [S] |
| Annex XIII Part A | The performance evaluation report must cover scientific validity, analytical and clinical performance | [S] |
| Specific bridging-study sample sizes, acceptance criteria | not set by these documents as far as read; *not verified* beyond the quoted text | – |

## (c) R lab

### Setting [A]

Randomised all-comers trial, n = 1200, biomarker prevalence 40%. Response rates: control 20%; treatment 50% in biomarker-positive, 20% in negative (no benefit). CTA sensitivity/specificity vs the true biomarker state 0.93/0.90, CDx 0.97/0.95, errors independent given the true state (a simplification; real errors correlate). The simulation knows the truth; reality does not.

```{r setting}
truth_cdx <- true_effect_cdx_pos()
truth_cta <- true_effect_cdx_pos(cdx = c(se = 0.93, sp = 0.90))
kable(data.frame(Population = c("True biomarker-positive", "CTA-positive (what the trial analysed)", "CDx-positive (who will be treated)"),
                 `Risk difference (treatment - control)` = round(c(0.30, truth_cta, truth_cdx), 3), check.names = FALSE),
      caption = "Dilution by false positives: the effect depends on how the population is selected")
```

### Concordance on the bridging samples (PPA/NPA/OPA)

```{r concordance}
set.seed(81)
d <- sim_trial(1200, miss = "MCAR", p_obs = 0.60)
b <- d[d$obs == 1, ]
a <- report_agreement(b$cdx == 1, b$cta == 1)
kable(data.frame(Measure = a$measure, `x/n` = paste0(a$x, "/", a$n), Estimate = round(100 * a$est, 1),
                 `Wilson 95% CI` = sprintf("%.1f - %.1f", 100 * a$lower, 100 * a$upper), check.names = FALSE),
      caption = sprintf("CDx vs CTA in %d bridging samples (%.0f%% of the trial)", nrow(b), 100 * mean(d$obs)))
```

The CTA is the **comparator**, not a reference: call these PPA/NPA/OPA (FDA 2007 logic, Day 5). The reported agreement is below 100% *even though both assays are fairly accurate*, because both have errors against the (unobservable) truth. [Y]

### Estimating efficacy in the CDx+ population when bridging samples are missing

Estimators of the risk difference among CDx+ subjects: **full** (impossible in practice: CDx known for all), **complete case** (only subjects with a sample), **IPW** (weights 1/P(sample | CTA, arm)), **multiple imputation** of the CDx result (logistic on CTA, arm, response and arm×response; Rubin's rules). Missingness mechanisms: **MCAR** (60% random), **MAR** (sample more likely when CTA+), **MNAR** (sample more likely when the CDx itself is positive), **MNAR_resp** (as MNAR, and among CDx+ subjects responders are more likely to have a retained sample).

```{r mc}
set.seed(82)
R <- 300
run <- function(miss) {
  out <- replicate(R, {
    d <- sim_trial(1200, miss = miss)
    e <- list(full = est_full(d), cc = est_cc(d), ipw = est_ipw(d), mi = est_mi(d, 10))
    unlist(lapply(e, function(v) c(v[["est"]], v[["se"]])))
  })
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("full", "cc", "ipw", "mi"), function(m) {
    est <- out[paste0(m, "1"), ]; se <- out[paste0(m, "2"), ]
    data.frame(Missingness = miss, Estimator = m, Bias = mean(est) - truth_cdx, RMSE = sqrt(mean((est - truth_cdx)^2)),
               Coverage = mean(abs(est - truth_cdx) <= 1.96 * se))
  }))
}
res <- rbind(run("MCAR"), run("MAR"), run("MNAR"), run("MNAR_resp"))
kable(res, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = sprintf("%d simulated trials per scenario; truth = %.3f", R, truth_cdx))
```

```{r mc-plot}
#| fig-height: 3.4
ggplot(res, aes(Estimator, Bias, fill = Estimator)) + geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Missingness) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(subtitle = "Bias in the CDx+ risk difference by missingness mechanism")
```

Reading [Y]:

- **MCAR/MAR**: all estimators are close to unbiased here; MI and IPW are the principled choices when availability depends on measured variables, and MI gains precision (smaller RMSE than complete case).
- **MNAR (availability depends on the CDx result only)**: complete case is *still unbiased*. The analysis population is "CDx+ subjects", and selection that depends only on the stratifying variable does not distort a comparison *within* that stratum. IPW and MI, which model missingness through the CTA, are the ones that drift (MI worst).
- **MNAR_resp (availability also depends on the outcome)**: now complete case (+0.032) and IPW (+0.026) are distorted, because responders are over-represented among retained samples. MI, which conditions on the outcome, is least affected here (−0.010) but is not protected in general: availability still depends on the CDx result itself. Only a sensitivity analysis can bracket the remaining risk.
- The imputation model needed the arm × response term: omitting it gave a visible bias in my check, because the drug works only in biomarker-positives.

The practical lesson is to **find out why samples are missing** before choosing the estimator, and to pre-specify the sensitivity analysis. [Y]

### Tipping-point sensitivity analysis (MNAR)

Assume a fraction `pi_miss` of the subjects without a sample are CDx+ (the observed fraction among those with a sample is the reference value), and see where the conclusion changes.

```{r tipping}
set.seed(83)
d <- sim_trial(1200, miss = "MNAR")
ref <- mean(d$cdx[d$obs == 1])
grid <- seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.05)
tp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(grid, function(p) { e <- est_tipping(d, p)
  data.frame(pi_miss = p, est = e[["est"]], lo = e[["est"]] - 1.96 * e[["se"]], hi = e[["est"]] + 1.96 * e[["se"]]) }))
c(observed_CDx_pos_fraction_in_bridging_set = ref, true_fraction = mean(d$cdx), fraction_among_missing = mean(d$cdx[d$obs == 0]))
ggplot(tp, aes(pi_miss, est)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = .2) + geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = truth_cdx, linetype = 3) + geom_vline(xintercept = ref, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Assumed CDx+ probability among subjects without a sample", y = "Risk difference in CDx+",
       subtitle = "dashed = observed fraction in bridging set; dotted = true effect") + theme_minimal()
```

```{r tipping-range}
c(est_min = min(tp$est), est_max = max(tp$est), lower_CI_min = min(tp$lo))
```

Across the whole grid the estimate stays well above zero (the minimum lower CI limit is shown above), so the conclusion is **robust to this assumption** in this dataset. A real report would state the range of assumptions examined and the point at which the conclusion would change (the tipping point), if there is one. [Y]

### Cross-check of the imputation with `mice`

```{r mice}
set.seed(84)
d <- sim_trial(1200, miss = "MAR")
d$cdx_m <- ifelse(d$obs == 1, d$cdx, NA)
d$ar <- d$arm * d$resp
imp <- mice(d[, c("cdx_m", "cta", "arm", "resp", "ar")], m = 20, method = c("logreg", "", "", "", ""), printFlag = FALSE)
mi_mice <- mean(sapply(seq_len(20), function(i) {
  x <- complete(imp, i); k <- x$cdx_m == 1; rd_est(x$arm[k], x$resp[k])[["est"]] }))
mi_mine <- est_mi(d, 40)[["est"]]
kable(data.frame(Method = c("hand MI", "mice (logreg)", "full information", "analytic truth"),
                 `Risk difference CDx+` = round(c(mi_mine, mi_mice, est_full(d)[["est"]], truth_cdx), 3), check.names = FALSE))
stopifnot(abs(mi_mine - mi_mice) < 0.03)
```

### Design: enrichment vs all-comers [A]

Same number *randomised* (n = 160): enrichment randomises CTA+ only (screening about 2.5 patients per randomised one); all-comers randomises everyone, so only about 43% of its patients are CTA+. Power for the effect in the CTA+ population, and power of the treatment × biomarker interaction test (only possible with all-comers).

```{r design}
set.seed(85)
nn <- 160
cmp_prop <- function(d) suppressWarnings(prop.test(table(factor(d$arm, 0:1), factor(d$resp, 0:1))[, 2:1])$p.value) < .05
pw_enrich <- function(reps = 600) mean(replicate(reps, {
  d <- sim_trial(ceiling(nn / 0.40) + 60, miss = "none"); cmp_prop(d[d$cta == 1, ][seq_len(nn), ]) }))
pw_all <- function(reps = 600) mean(replicate(reps, { d <- sim_trial(nn, miss = "none"); cmp_prop(d[d$cta == 1, ]) }))
inter <- function(reps = 600) mean(replicate(reps, {
  d <- sim_trial(nn, miss = "none"); f <- glm(resp ~ arm * cta, binomial, d)
  summary(f)$coefficients["arm:cta", 4] < .05 }))
kable(data.frame(
  Design = c("Enrichment: effect in CTA+ (160 randomised CTA+)",
             "All-comers (160 randomised): effect in its CTA+ subgroup",
             "All-comers (160 randomised): treatment x CTA interaction"),
  Power = c(pw_enrich(), pw_all(), inter())), digits = 3)
```

Enrichment gives the most power for the effect in the selected population but no information on biomarker-negatives (and none on CTA false negatives); the all-comers design costs power but supports the claim that benefit is *restricted* to biomarker-positives and is the base for a CDx labelling decision. [Y]

### Estimand sketch for a CDx claim (ICH E9(R1) vocabulary by analogy) [Y]

| Attribute | Choice here |
|---|---|
| Population | Patients who test CDx+ with the final IVD in the intended-use setting |
| Treatment | Drug vs control, treatment-policy |
| Variable | Response (or time to event) |
| Intercurrent events | Discontinuation, switching: treatment-policy or hypothetical, pre-specified |
| Summary measure | Risk difference or ratio / hazard ratio in CDx+ |
| Bridging-specific | How subjects without CDx samples are handled (IPW / MI / bounds), analysis of CTA-CDx discordant subjects |
